claim: For \(\lambda>0\) and either \(2\le p\le q\le\infty\) or \(1\le p\le q\le2\), let \(X_{\lambda,p,q}=(\mathbb R^2,N_{\lambda,p,q})\), where \(N_{\lambda,p,q}(x,y)=\bigl(\|(x,y)\|_p^2+\lambda\|(x,y)\|_q^2\bigr)^{1/2}\). Then \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X_{\lambda,p,q},\ell_2^2)^2=C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X_{\lambda,p,q})\), and this common value is \(\frac{2(1+\lambda)}{2^{2/p}+\lambda2^{2/q}}\) when \(2\le p\le q\le\infty\), while it is \(\frac{2^{2/p}+\lambda2^{2/q}}{2(1+\lambda)}\) when \(1\le p\le q\le2\), with the convention \(2^{2/\infty}=1\).

correctness.rationale: The proof optimizes over every linear isomorphism \(T\): signed-permutation averaging of \(T^\mathsf{T}T\) forces a scalar comparison and makes the identity radial ratio optimal. Sharp Euclidean-circle extrema of \(\ell_r\) norms then give both formulas. The source's Example 4.2 independently gives the identical expressions for \(C_{\mathrm{NJ}}\). The endpoint cases \(p=q=2\), \(p=q=1\), and \(p=q=\infty\) agree with the classical Euclidean, diamond, and square distances.

value.rationale: The result computes an exact standard affine invariant for a natural three-parameter family already used to test exact Banach-space geometric constants. It also gives the structural identity \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}^2=C_{\mathrm{NJ}}\) over two complete regimes and explains it by a reusable signed-permutation symmetry reduction, rather than by an arbitrary parameter slice.
